gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much energy EcoFlow units actually delivered in named lab tests: StorageReview measured 910 Wh from the 1,024 Wh DELTA 3 Plus (88.9%), 1,800 Wh from the 2,048 Wh DELTA 2 Max (about 88%) and 210 Wh from the 245 Wh RIVER 3 (about 86%), and OutdoorGearLab measured 870 Wh from the 1,024 Wh DELTA 3 (85%).
standout_why: The solarkontor.de guide gives only spec-style claims and no measured capacity, efficiency, noise or idle figures. The explorersweb.com DELTA Max piece is sponsored by EcoFlow, quotes only the maker's specs and covers a discontinued model. The two notebookcheck.net items (RIVER 3 Plus launch, dated 2025-03-27; Trail 300 DC launch) are launch news with the maker's figures and no tests. The techradar.com tag page shows no figures. The trailandkale.com review returned 404. The tech.yahoo.com DELTA 3 Plus review (a How-To Geek review, 8/10) returned 403, so I could not check whether it measured anything. The rei.com and shopsolarkits.com result pages are retailer listings and were not opened. None of the pages I could open gives measured usable Wh, round-trip efficiency, UPS switchover time or idle draw for any EcoFlow model.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Across the line, named labs got 85–89% of rated capacity at the outlet, so a shopper should size the purchase by about 0.85 × rated Wh: a DELTA 3 or DELTA 3 Plus gives roughly 870–910 Wh, and a RIVER 3 roughly 210 Wh. For a home or office UPS, the DELTA 3 Plus has a measured switchover of just over 8 ms (StorageReview), which supports it over the RIVER 3, whose switchover nobody measured. For multi-day standby, The Solar Lab measured about 22 W idle draw on the DELTA 3 Ultra, which burns a meaningful share of its 3,072 Wh over days. Plug-to-outlet round trip is about 76–78% on all three StorageReview units, so efficiency does not separate the models.
